Donate | First 100 Days | Support Donate Now Home As many of you already know, I have been a commissioner for the City of Miami since September 3rd, 1996. For over a decade, it has been a privilege and an honor to serve the residents of our great City. Today, I ask for your support and vote as a candidate for Mayor of Miami. It is important you understand how profound my devotion to this City really is. I believe Miami excels because it has great residents, who constantly push for a better quality of life. However, in the years past, the vision for our City has focused on an uncompromising dream of a bustling metropolis. Development and growth tightly grips the reins of our political machine. This is not greatness but rather a manifestation of affluence. When I speak of our great City, I do not envision a metropolis. I see a City whose residents are proud to call Miami their home. A City where its people feel safe, and where there is a sense of community and responsibility. Miami belongs to its residents and we as elected officials must answer to all residents, not just the wealthy and powerful. The time has come for us to reclaim our City. I regret to inform you that for years now residents have taken a back seat to special interests under the guise of progress and development. At times, I have been the lone voice against these special interests. I have persistently tried to remind my colleagues of our responsibility to you, the residents, of this great City. As such, my mayoral campaign is not about slogans and catch phrases. I ask only that you look at my record as a leader. Something that I would like to bring about as part of this campaign is my ardent discontent with the two-minute rule. For those of you unfamiliar with this rule, the two minutes refers to the time allotted to residents when speaking before the City of Miami Commission. I am totally against this time limit because residents are only granted two minutes, while special interests receive hours of attention before commissioners behind closed doors. How can a city government preach democratic ideologies, if the very fiber...its people...are allowed only two minutes to voice concerns? Help me take back our great City. Help me prove, once and for all, we cannot measure the success of a city by the height of its buildings, but rather by the quality of life of its residents. Help me prove the solutions to our problems are not in higher taxes and inefficient projects tailored to fill the pockets of the affluent. I promise we can do more with less. We shall no longer spend massive amounts of public funds on unproductive development. We can do what is right not only for today's residents, but for our children's future. My vision for Miami is simple. I picture a City where all residents and visitors can walk the streets safely at night. A City where one can decide to take an early morning jog without the slightest bit of hesitation or fear. This great city should be a place where our children can play on our baseball fields and basketball courts without trepidation. A place we can guarantee is clean and pleasant. But most importantly, a city that uses your hard earned tax money to light our streets, pave our roads and educate our youth. My critics claim I lack vision because I speak of potholes and garbage collection. But I tell you now: I do not lack vision. I believe as public servants we have an obligation to provide our residents with the expected services they pay for. I understand that unfortunately this has become a novel concept, which many of my critics do not value. But as a resident, a father and a grandfather, I recognize the meaning behind quality of life. So this has become my commitment to you, the residents of this great City. As your mayor, I promise to focus on our basic necessities and more importantly to use our financial resources to enhance our City from within. We need to focus on making Miami a more efficient, clean, friendly and secure city. Instead of spending millions on masking problems, let us fix them. In the coming months, I will present my vision for this great City. But like always, I welcome and encourage your thoughts and opinions. I implore your help in my mission to take back our great City and make it a place we are all proud and grateful to call home. Since January 2013, we have begun living in a better Stockton. Here are some of the changes that have happened in our city: Homicides are down by 60%. Non-fatal shootings are down by 50%. Josh Lee has... 27 views 0 comments Post not marked as liked ABOUT ME Here is what you can expect from Josh A TEAM APPROACH TO GOVERNMENT I believe it is foolish to think that one person has all the best ideas or all the connections to make things happen. Having one person run everything is not leadership; it is a dictatorship. ​ If elected, my administration will use a team approach. We have assembled an Advisory Committee made up of different people from around the Vinita area. Each person wants to see our community prosper. Each person is committed to helping come up with ideas to make our city better. Each person is committed to using their unique connections to help our ideas thrive. If we win the election, this committee will become the Mayor's Advisory Committee, and it will hold monthly meetings to plan for the future. Anyone with unique connections, new ideas, or just a heartfelt commitment to helping make Vinita a better place to live, work, and raise a family is welcome to serve on this advisory committee. A COMMITMENT TO GROWTH Vinita is shrinking. 95% of towns similar to our size are growing faster than us since 2000. This is not a trend we can sustain any longer. We must get serious about bringing in new business and helping our current businesses be successful and stay open. If elected I promise to support our local businesses, encourage and support entrepreneurs, help our local workforce, attract new businesses, and make our industrial park attractive to businesses. PROTECTION OF YOUR LIBERTIES No ideal is more central to the founding of the United States than that of individual liberties. It is a central component of what we are as human beings. Liberty is directly related to our self-worth and our dignity. Fear should not so easily strip us of our liberty, our dignity, as it has done recently, right here in Vinita. My opponent declared it a crime for citizens to go outside their homes during certain hours; made it a crime to attend church; made it a crime for pastors to open church doors; made it a crime to go to a loved one's house; made it a crime for business owners to open their doors and try to earn a living. His actions are unforgivable. If elected, I will never take away your liberties. I pledge to never close down your business and to never take away your ability to earn a living and feed your family. Most importantly, I will never interfere with your ability to attend church and worship when you please and as you please. I will also respect the 2nd Amendment to the United States Constitution, and I will see to it that the City of Vinita will not enforce any state or federal laws that are unconstitutional and violative of your 2nd Amendment Rights. Vinita will be a 2nd Amendment safe haven, just as our founding fathers originally intended. TRANSPARENCY If elected as Mayor of Vinita, there will be a new attitude brought to City Hall. This new attitude will serve as a stern reminder to all elected officials of whom they work for - the citizens. Vinita's government will be transparent and will not operate under the cloak of secrecy. Meeting agendas will clearly state what is going to be discussed. Every council meeting will be streamed online so people may see how their city is being run. Agendas will be available on the website with the same information the councilors see and will no longer be hidden from the public. We will use fewer executive sessions, so there is less discussion hidden from the citizens. When we do use executive sessions, they will be clearly described, so every citizen will know exactly what topic is being discussed - no more vagueness. We will no longer prohibit city councilors from talking to city employees. We will obtain up-to-date training for all city leaders on the Oklahoma Open Records Act and the Oklahoma Open Meeting Act. Vinita will respect the importance of an open and transparent government. ​ If elected, I will seek changes to our municipal code to require all elected officials to complete a Personal Financial Disclosure Statement as provided for by the Oklahoma Ethics Commission, disclosing all financial interests that they have. Our citizens have a right to know what business interests their elected officials have and be aware of conflicts of interest between their public duties and private economic interests. If our elected officials stand to gain from actions taken by them or not taken by them, then that information can not remain secret. Elected officials should be in their position to serve the citizens, not to profit from it. FISCAL RESPONSABILITY I believe that the City of Vinita wastes money in areas that do not directly help the citizens of Vinita. My parents formed my belief that all life is sacred and that everyone should be treated fairly and with respect. My father was a Marine who fought at Iwo Jima. He taught me to honor this nation and respect its laws and those who risk their lives to protect us and to enforce our laws. I was taught to spend money wisely so you can take care of what is most important first. And, I learned the virtues of small government and personal responsibility. FOCUSED ON LUBBOCK’S FUTURE Keeping Property Taxes Low These past few years of inflation and stagnant wages have been hard on household budgets. The City Council is not being responsible to our taxpayers if it ignores this when setting the property tax rate, especially when house appraisals have shot up through the roof. It is no secret that drug and gang related crime is making us all feel less safe in our homes and neighborhoods. Our next police chief must have a clear plan for reducing violent crime. Our police and firefighters must have the pay and support they need to keep their ranks filled. Protecting our Neighborhoods Our neighborhoods are where we live and raise our families. I have not and will not vote for zoning changes allowing big developers to build projects that disrupt our neighborhoods. Our small businesses are essential and can’t be shut down again. I will make sure Lubbock continues to be an attractive place for starting and growing a business with streamlined permitting and fewer regulations and by maintaining our low cost of living with low property taxes. Improving our Streets and Essential Services Streets, sewers and water lines are basic and essential services our citizens depend on. I will make repairing and maintaining them a budget priority over other non-essential services. Water for our Future Water is vital to our future. I will work to make sure our planned Canyon Lake 7 stays on the fast track to completion. And, I’ll make sure we focus on bringing low-water consumption businesses to town and continue our highly successful efforts to reduce our residential water consumption. family MY FAMILY Cindy and I have been married for 40 years. Joe McComb Joe McComb Just another WordPress site Home About Joe News/Media Volunteer Donate Contact On Tuesday, Nov. 8, 2016, Corpus Christi voters decided overwhelmingly that they wanted to move away from politics as usual and elected a new mayor and four new council members to serve on the Corpus Christi City Council. Thirty seven days later the newly elected mayor resigned. Voters in November indicated to me through their votes that they want to see change. They want: To wake up not having to worry about another water boil. To see measurable improvements over the next two years in streets with approved bond projects underway and completed. Careful management of resources and tax dollars. Improved communications between the city and citizens. A mayor who will unify the many diverse groups in our city and make the tough decisions I think I have shown that you can trust me to achieve your goals and that is why I am running for Mayor of Corpus Christi in the May 6th election. Many of you know me. In addition to being active in our community for decades, I served two terms on city council in the late 1980s and 1990s. I was a Nueces County Commissioner from 1995 to 2002 and from 2011 to 2014. I understand city government and how it needs to work to benefit all of the people. Last year, after recognizing the issues facing our city, I decided to run for an at-large seat on our city council. You elected me with more votes than any other at-large candidate. I thank you and appreciate your confidence. Now I am asking for your help again. I can’t promise you that I can solve all the problems immediately, but I can promise you that I will work to make Corpus Christi the best city it can be. I will be a leader with integrity who you can trust. It is time that we tackled the issues facing our city and make sure you are provided the right kind of basic services while improving our infrastructure and economic development efforts. I understand that at some point you have to forget all the thrills and frills and get back to the basics. As your mayor, I promise you that I will: Take care of business Deliver what I promise Hear everybody’s concerns Be willing to make decisions. I will also continue to prioritize finding the correct funding mechanisms for street repairs; ensure the integrity of the water, wastewater and storm water systems; and make adjustments in the budget to prioritize spending. Working together we can solve any issue facing our city and keep Corpus Christi the best place in the United States to live, work and raise our families. Recent Posts Hello world! What a wonderful place to live! What a privilege to be your Mayor! The Sears Centre opened in October 2006. It features sporting events, concerts and other entertainment venues. Some of our local high schools will do their graduation events there; no more worry about the weather. Cabela's, an indoor-outdoor water park with a hotel and a 9,000 seat outdoor concert park are scheduled to be built during the next two years. Our new Poplar Creek Crossing Shopping Center at the corner of routes 59 and 72 is a wonderful addition to our retail choices, and I hope you all shop there as often as possible - your local sales taxes help our Village. We are continuing our local retail redevelopment efforts in our older shopping areas also. The road reconstruction program in Hoffman Estates is in full gear. A feasability analysis for the STAR Line, our proposed suburb-to-suburb rail line is scheduled for completion by next spring.
